hints: Resolve vertically in equilibrium: $P\sin\theta + 20 = (36 + 24)\sin\alpha = 60(0.6) = 36\text{ N}$, giving $P\sin\theta = 16\text{ N}$.
Divide the components to find $\theta = \arctan(16 / 9.6)$, and use Pythagoras theorem to find $P = \sqrt{9.6^2 + 16^2}$.
walkthrough:
Determine the exact cosine value from $\sin\alpha = 0.6$:
$$\cos\alpha = \sqrt{1 - 0.6^2} = 0.8$$

Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium:
$$P\cos\theta = (36 - 24)\cos\alpha = 12(0.8) = 9.6\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium:
$$P\sin\theta + 20 = 24\sin\alpha + 36\sin\alpha = 60(0.6) = 36\text{ N}$$
$$P\sin\theta = 36 - 20 = 16\text{ N}$$

Solve for magnitude $P$ and angle $\theta$:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{16}{9.6} = \frac{5}{3} \implies \theta = \arctan\left(\frac{5}{3}\right) \approx 59.0^\circ$$
$$P = \sqrt{9.6^2 + 16^2} = \sqrt{92.16 + 256} = \sqrt{348.16} \approx 18.7\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.Resolving Forces Along Chosen Axes: Resolves horizontally to get $P\cos\theta = 9.6\text{ N}$ and vertically to get $P\sin\theta = 16\text{ N}$, obtaining $P = 18.7\text{ N}$ and $\theta = 59.0^\circ$.

teacher_walkthrough:
First, determine the trigonometric ratios for angle $\alpha$:
$$\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6$$
$$\cos\alpha = \sqrt{1 - \sin^2\alpha} = \sqrt{1 - 0.36} = \sqrt{0.64} = 0.8$$

State the conditions for coplanar equilibrium:
$$\sum F_x = 0\quad\text{and}\quad \sum F_y = 0$$

Resolve all forces along the horizontal $x$-axis:
$$P\cos\theta + 24\cos\alpha - 36\cos\alpha = 0$$
$$P\cos\theta - (36 - 24)\cos\alpha = 0$$
$$P\cos\theta = 12\cos\alpha = 12(0.8) = 9.6\text{ N}$$

Resolve all forces along the vertical $y$-axis:
$$P\sin\theta + 20 - 24\sin\alpha - 36\sin\alpha = 0$$
$$P\sin\theta + 20 - (24 + 36)\sin\alpha = 0$$
$$P\sin\theta + 20 - 60(0.6) = 0$$
$$P\sin\theta + 20 - 36 = 0$$
$$P\sin\theta = 16\text{ N}$$

Divide the vertical equation by the horizontal equation to find the direction angle $\theta$:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{P\sin\theta}{P\cos\theta} = \frac{16}{9.6} = \frac{5}{3} \approx 1.66667$$
$$\theta = \arctan(1.66667) \approx 59.036^\circ$$
Rounding to one decimal place gives $\theta = 59.0^\circ$.

Calculate the magnitude $P$ using the Pythagorean theorem:
$$P = \sqrt{(P\cos\theta)^2 + (P\sin\theta)^2} = \sqrt{(9.6)^2 + (16)^2}$$
$$P = \sqrt{92.16 + 256} = \sqrt{348.16} \approx 18.659\text{ N}$$
Rounding to three significant figures gives $P = 18.7\text{ N}$.
Thus $P = 18.7\text{ N}$ and $\theta = 59.0^\circ$.
